subject.title: fix(discord): default account env fallback when accounts.default.token is blank

question: Should a shipped blank `channels.discord.accounts.default.token` inherit top-level/env fallback, or remain an explicit default-account opt-out?
rationale: The PR's central behavior is plausible and matches the documented default-account env fallback, but it changes a shipped credential-selection edge case that some operators may have used as an opt-out.

options.title: Default blank inherits fallback
options.body: Treat a blank default-account token as absent, keep non-default blank token opt-out and SecretRef `configured_unavailable`, and align resolver, inspect, and setup status around that contract.

options.title: Blank remains opt-out
options.body: Keep the shipped blank-token behavior, close or rework this PR, and fix docs/setup/doctor so env fallback does not depend on blank default stubs.

options.title: Require explicit disable path
options.body: Adopt fallback for blank default tokens only with a clearly tested disable path such as `enabled: false` and release-note context for existing operators.

recommendation.title: Default blank inherits fallback
recommendation.body: Treat a blank default-account token as absent, keep non-default blank token opt-out and SecretRef `configured_unavailable`, and align resolver, inspect, and setup status around that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work touched both account-token inspection and setup status, the two surfaces that must be aligned with the resolver decision.
